div.p: SmartphoneKey is an access management platform. It combines the Admin Panel, Wallet keys and NFC cards, SmartphoneKey readers with a built-in access controller, and connected-device scenarios, so teams can manage access across their sites.
No. The readers are part of the system. The platform also covers sites, people and their access, cards and digital keys, events and device status.

div.h3: What does a resident need to enter?
div.p: Whatever the site issues to them: a Wallet key on a supported phone, or an NFC card. They can manage their keys in the SmartphoneKey app on Android or iPhone. Visitors use the QR code at the entrance.

div.p: Add residents, staff and contractors to the site they belong to and choose the doors they can open. For any site, review its people, keys, cards, readers and related devices.

Issue Wallet keys, manage NFC cards and give temporary access where it is supported. When access is no longer needed, revoke it and check that each reader has applied the change.

section.p: A contractor needs access to a service room. The administrator chooses the site and the doors, issues a key or card, and checks that the readers have confirmed it. When the work ends, the administrator revokes the access and checks again.

Review activity and audit records for each site. Device monitoring shows readers that have lost their connection and operations that failed. You can configure alerts for supported device events; they do not replace an agreed support process.

Some changes wait until the reader reconnects. Pending means the reader has not confirmed the change yet. Whether keys and cards keep working at the door during an outage depends on the device and its configuration.
A revocation made while the reader is offline is not in effect on that reader until it confirms the change.

div.h3: Can I manage more than one site?
div.p: Yes. Each site is managed on its own, and you can give administrators access to the sites they look after. The actions available depend on account permissions and configured services.

div.h3: What happens to a key change while a reader is offline?
div.p: Some changes stay pending until the reader reconnects. Check the status: a revocation that is still pending is not yet in effect on that reader.

section.p: A Matter label does not mean every device offers the same functions. A scenario can use only what each commissioned device reports and its firmware supports. Each scenario runs on one hub and the devices commissioned to it.

section.h2: Check that the hub applied the change
section.p: The Admin Panel shows whether a scenario change is waiting for the hub, applied or rejected. Until the hub applies an edit, the version already on the hub keeps running.

div.h3: Does SmartphoneKey work with every Matter device?
div.p: It depends on the device type, the capabilities it reports, its firmware and your configuration. Check the functions your scenario needs rather than assuming every Matter device offers them.

div.h3: Can one scenario use devices on two hubs?
div.p: No. Each scenario currently belongs to one hub and the devices commissioned to it. Plan each scenario around the hub that controls the devices it needs.

section.p: AI Concierge uses AI to understand the request. Access rules on the server decide whether it can go ahead, so a persuasive conversation does not grant access.
